notesStmt.note: Whitman's note on this manuscript, "May, 1885," would seem to pinpoint the date of its creation quite precisely. Given the poem's first publication two and a half years later, however, it also seems possible that the note was added later and is in error.

The handwritten alterations on this proof slip were incorporated into the first publication of "You Lingering Sparse Leaves of Me," in the November 1887 issue of Lippincott's Magazine. There, the poem was part of a four-poem sequence titled "November Boughs." That grouping was not maintained when the poem was further revised and printed in November Boughs (1888) and in the "Sands at Seventy" annex to Leaves of Grass (1891-1892).

body.head:
YOU LINGERING SPARSE LEAVES
OF ME.

lg.l: You lingering sparse leaves of me on bare December?November boughs,
And I some well-shown tree of field or orchard-row;

You tokens diminute and lorn—(not now the flush of May.—
nor July clover bloom,—no fruits of August now;)

You pallid little banners, remnants valueless—you overstay'd
of time,
Yet my soul-dearest leaves—the hardiest and the last.
